answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where a trusted beacon broadcasts a unique identifier to all participants. Each agent maintains a localized atlas of known peers, updated via a zephyr-like gossip protocol. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to expend resources proportional to the number of fake identities, as each would require a distinct identifier and storage in the atlas, making large-scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
